name: XT30 male connector, solder cups (Amass XT30U-M)
blurb: The small yellow two-pin battery connector, 15 A. This is the half with the two pins inside a shroud; wires are soldered into the cups at the back and it only plugs in one way round.

pins.note: The cup at the end of the housing with the two cut-off (chamfered) corners. A small - is moulded into the housing beside it: go by that mark.

The cup at the square end of the housing, marked + in the plastic. This file gives the pin no voltage: it carries whatever is on the other half. Slide heat-shrink over the wire before soldering, and solder with the other half plugged in so the heat does not let the pin drift in the plastic.

search: XT30U male female pair genuine Amass

verify: From the Amass XT30U-M drawing: housing face 10.20 x 5.20 mm, 13.70 mm long overall of which the solder cups are the last 3.00 mm, pins 5.00 mm apart; 15 A continuous, 30 A peak, 500 V DC, 18 AWG wire recommended. The Amass drawing shows the shape (one end square, one end with cut corners) but prints no polarity. That the cut-corner end is - and the square end is + is from the KiCad footprint of the same part, which marks pad 1 at the chamfered end '-' and pad 2 '+'; the housing itself carries moulded + and - marks, and those decide. Male here means the pins: on XT connectors the half with the pins sits in the shroud, and by convention it goes on the load side, the socket half (XT30U-F) on the battery, so the live side has no exposed pins. Drawn lying flat with the mating end at y = 0 and the cups at the back; the pads on a carrier PCB are 2.7 mm holes 5.0 mm apart with the connector standing up. No port is defined: add an opening by hand if the connector must sit in a case wall. Clones vary in how tightly they mate.
